subject: English
passage: Dr. James Okafor and Dr. Sarah Nakamura collected data from 298 fitness app users to identify factors that influence users to opt for premium versions of fitness apps, like Peloton. They hypothesized that interface usability (the perceived ease with which an app's features can be navigated and used by a consumer) would be positively correlated with users' intentions to adopt premium versions. The researchers asked participants to rate statements such as "I find premium fitness apps easy to navigate and use." They found that, indeed, interface usability positively influences the intention to adopt premium fitness app versions, which suggests that ______
prompt: Which choice most logically completes the text?

choices.A: the statement "I find premium fitness apps easy to navigate and use" is not a reliable measure of interface usability.
choices.B: participants who strongly agreed with the statement "I find premium fitness apps easy to navigate and use" were more likely to express loyalty to Peloton than to other fitness apps.
choices.C: users' intentions to pay for premium fitness apps are probably unaffected by factors other than interface usability.
choices.D: it may be advantageous for fitness app companies to try to influence the extent to which potential users perceive the use of the premium version as effortless.

explanation: Choice D is the best answer because it provides the most logical practical implication of the research findings. The study establishes that interface usability (perceived ease of use) is positively correlated with users' intentions to adopt premium fitness apps. If ease-of-use perception influences adoption intention, then companies would logically benefit from making their premium versions appear easy to use. Choice D appropriately translates this research finding into a business application using qualified language ('may be advantageous').
